rules.penalty_amount_rule: How penalty amounts are counted: each row counts the cash the defendant actually paid (penalties, restitution, damages, fees). Press-release headline figures are often larger because they include debt relief, forgiven debt or rent, bill credits, conditional amounts, or proposed penalties that can still be contested. Those parts are not counted here. Every one is listed under Amounts not counted, with the headline figure, what we counted, the reason and the source. Where a release does not state the split between cash and relief, the case is left out of the totals and listed there.
rules.duplicate_rule: How duplicates are counted: when two records describe the same payment, it is counted once. A record is left out only when a primary document read for this ledger shows the dollars are the same. When that document cannot be read, a strong match is still counted once and is marked 'possible duplicate, counted once until verified'. Records for different payments are all counted, even when the amounts are equal. Every record left out stays in the gross figure and is listed under Amounts not counted, with the document behind the call.
rules.shared_total_rule: How shared totals are counted: when several defendants pay one total, each company counts only the share its primary document states. If the document gives a total and no split, and the payers include anyone outside the one company (another company, or individuals such as owners), the total is counted for no company: it stays in the gross figure and is listed under Amounts not counted. Where every payer named belongs to the one company, the whole total counts once, in full, for that company.
